blocks.text: An ester is hydrolyzed slowly to a carboxylic acid and an alcohol (or a phenol). The reaction is either acid or base-catalyzed. The hydrolysis of aliphatic esters is already discussed earlier in this chapter. Aromatic esters are also hydrolysed in the same manner, giving aryl carboxylic acids and alcohols or phenol.

blocks.alt: Two equations with H+ / OH- over the arrow. Ethyl benzoate (a benzene ring with C(=O)-O-C2H5) + H2O gives benzoic acid (ring with C(=O)-OH) + C2H5OH, ethanol. Methyl benzoate (ring with C(=O)-O-CH3) + H2O gives benzoic acid + CH3OH, methanol.
blocks.caption: Hydrolysis of ethyl benzoate and methyl benzoate (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 114).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed hydrolysis equations have no water on the left; + H₂O is added in the drawing. The labels 'ethylbenzoate' and 'methylbenzoate' are written ethyl benzoate and methyl benzoate.
